issues.description: The commented example code in the template Main.java instantiates Seal, Pig, and Goat with two constructor parameters (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the problem UML and the solution implement Animal and its subclasses with a single-parameter constructor (only name). This mismatch can confuse students about the expected constructor signatures and which attributes they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the example code in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java consistent with the UML/specification by using single-argument constructors (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle")). Alternatively, if two-argument constructors are intended, update the UML/problem text and the solution to include the additional attribute and corresponding constructor parameter.

issues.description: Inconsistent constructor signatures for Animal subclasses: the Problem Statement requires each animal to have a constructor that initializes its attributes (the only common attribute being name), and the Solution implements single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal(String name)). However, the Template's Main.java instantiates animals using two-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), suggesting a different constructor signature. This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor parameters and lead to compilation errors or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem and solution by changing the example instantiations in template/Main.java to use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal seal = new Seal("Clarabelle"); Pig pig = new Pig("Doodle"); Goat goat = new Goat("Buttinsky");). Alternatively, if a second attribute was intended, update the problem statement and solution to document and implement that additional attribute consistently (or provide overloaded constructors).
